fatal_errors: Identifies a coherent HEA interface as the transition material, whereas the transition was observed in the λ = 16 nm Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer containing semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces with misfit dislocations.
Replaces room-temperature nanoindentation creep experiments with an unsupported high-temperature molecular-dynamics scenario.
Invents temperature, stress, and percentage creep-rate values that are absent from the target evidence.
Uses an incoherent-interface baseline rather than the coherent M8 and grain-boundary-dominated M32/M80 experimental baselines.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes that interface coherency can alter competition between dislocation motion and diffusion-mediated creep, but it gets the decisive interface state wrong. The reported transition and strongest creep resistance occur in the λ = 16 nm semicoherent multilayer, where misfit-dislocation-mediated blocking and pileup are proposed to generate localized stress and possibly interfacial amorphization, enabling atomic diffusion or interface slip. Coherent M8 instead remains predominantly dislocation-mediated. The generated high-temperature MD conditions, quantitative creep-rate reduction, and falsification threshold have no supporting evidence and conflict with the room-temperature, 5 mN nanoindentation study.
